title: Solids, Liquids and Gases
seo_title: Year 4 Science: Solids, Liquids and Gases Worksheets (States of Matter)
standard_text: Compare and group materials together, according to whether they are solids, liquids or gases.
meta_desc: Free Year 4 science worksheets on solids, liquids and gases: grouping materials, properties of each state, particles, tricky materials and the mass of gases. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Solids keep their shape, liquids flow, gases spread out to fill a space.
body_html:
How to think about it

Materials can be solids, liquids or gases.

  • Solids keep their shape and cannot be squashed. Liquids flow and take the shape of their container. Gases spread out to fill any space and can be squashed.
  • Particles: packed and fixed in solids; close but sliding in liquids; far apart and fast in gases.
  • Tricky ones: sand and sugar are solids (each grain keeps its shape); honey is a liquid; gases have mass.
Example

Sand pours. Solid or liquid?

Each grain keeps its shape

Answer: solid

Example

A gas is let out of a jar. What happens?

Gas particles spread out

Answer: it fills the room

Common mistakes

  • Thinking sand is a liquid because it pours.
  • Thinking gases have no mass.
  • Thinking honey is a solid because it is thick.

faq.q: What is the difference between solids, liquids and gases?
faq.a: Solids keep their own shape. Liquids flow and take the shape of their container. Gases spread out to fill any container and can be squashed.

faq.q: Is sand a solid or a liquid?
faq.a: A solid. It pours, but each grain is a tiny solid that keeps its shape.
Yes. Gases have mass. A pumped-up ball weighs more than a flat one, and a fizzy drink gets lighter as its gas escapes.
